claims.text: A modest amount of Al doping followed by thermal treatment can induce L12 precipitates in magnetic high-entropy alloys.
Al doping combined with L12-forming thermal treatment will increase the coercive field.
L12 precipitates increase coercivity by pinning magnetic domain walls.
The initial alloy is homogeneous and lacks significant secondary-phase precipitates.
The intervention is controlled Al doping followed by an annealing process intended to precipitate an ordered L12 phase.
Under suitable processing conditions, Al promotes formation of L12 precipitates.
The relevant structural mediator is a well-dispersed population of L12 precipitates in the matrix.
L12 precipitates act as pinning sites that impede magnetic-domain-wall motion.
Impeded domain-wall motion increases the coercive field.
The Al-doped and annealed sample will have a higher coercive field than a baseline without Al doping and L12 precipitates.
The effect is expected at ambient-temperature magnetic measurement conditions.
The effect should extend to high-entropy alloys with similar base compositions and thermal histories conducive to L12 formation.
The effect may not occur when alloy composition or processing does not support L12-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The boundary excludes conditions that do not support L12 formation, but the falsification rule treats failure to observe L12 precipitates as falsifying the hypothesis. Failure to produce the stipulated mediator would instead show that the intervention or processing conditions were unsuccessful, not decisively refute the proposed pinning mechanism.
